name: Slow-Moving Vehicle emblem
spec: fluorescent orange triangle with a dark red reflective border, point up
meaning: The vehicle ahead moves at 25 mph or less; slow down well back.

snippets.back: The slow-moving-vehicle emblem is required on vehicles traveling at twenty-five miles per hour or less.
The slow-moving-vehicle emblem is an orange reflective triangle edged in red.
The same passing steps apply when you pass slow-moving motorcycles, bicycles and mopeds.
A reflective orange triangle on the back of a vehicle marks it as built to travel slower than twenty-five miles per hour.

You may pass a slow-moving bicyclist in a no-passing zone if you can do so safely, whereas stopping, parking, or driving in a designated bicycle path or lane is prohibited unless entering or leaving an alley or driveway, performing official duties, following a police officer's direction, or facing an emergency, while yielding to bicycles.
A slow-moving-vehicle emblem identifies a vehicle traveling at twenty-five miles per hour or less, requiring adjustment of speed or position around it.
The slow-moving-vehicle emblem is an orange fluorescent and reflective triangle; on seeing it, slow promptly and proceed carefully.
The slow-moving-vehicle emblem identifies a vehicle traveling below twenty-five miles per hour under the handbook's definition.

result.summary: Spec of orange fluorescent/reflective triangle edged in red and meaning of 25 mph or less requiring slowing are stated in snippets.
